text:
maria: Quick Q — seeing 401s calling hosted API from my mac dev env. Set API_KEY in .env and add header `Authorization: Basic <base64>`. Anyone run into trailing-newline or padding issues?
aj: Are you doing `echo $API_KEY | base64` or using pbpaste/pbcopy? Newlines often sneak in. Use `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | base64` instead of `echo`.
maria: Ah — Dockerfile was doing `echo $API_KEY | base64`. I'll try printf. Also, do Node examples need the trailing colon for basic auth? Some snippets omit it.
samir: Yes include the colon. Basic auth encodes `username:password`. For API key as username with empty password you must do `Buffer.from(apiKey + ':').toString('base64')`. Example:
```
// Node
const header = 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(API_KEY + ':', 'utf8').toString('base64')
```
Also trim any whitespace if you're unsure: `.trim()`.
aj: For curl use: `-H "Authorization: Basic $(printf %s "$API_KEY:" | base64)"` — avoids `echo` newline.
devx-bot: FYI: guidance + snippets are in the devex FAQ: https://redwood.dev/docs/auth — use the 'Basic auth with API key' section :mag:
sre-rachel: Watch CI secrets too — GH runners sometimes add newlines when someone writes secrets via echo. In workflows prefer `echo -n "$SECRET"` or set via UI. Also base64 on Windows can behave differently (PowerShell writes CRLF) — prefer `Set-Content -NoNewline` or strip CRLF before encoding.
maria: Confirmed — printf + including colon fixed the 401. One follow-up: streaming endpoints (chat/stream) still threw 'connection reset' when header had a trailing space. Are streaming endpoints sensitive to that?
samir: Streaming doesn't change header parsing — any stray whitespace in header value can break auth on some proxies/load-balancers. Best to canonicalize header by trimming on client side. If you see connection resets, also check keepalive and whether intermediate proxy strips keepalive on HTTP/1.1.
aj: I'll add a short snippet and a note about CRLF/newline gotchas to the devex FAQ.
maria: Thanks — will close this thread after you push the snippet :thumbsup:
